the_new_class_measured_and_reproduced.finding: BC-07 FAIL at S9, causal_stage COMPOSING, section api_reference: "internal narration 'generated by'". The exact rendered text (README.md line 262, content_units.json slot type:public_symbol:aspose.page.ps.clipper.outpt): "OutPt stores a point in the output polygon generated by the clipping operation."
the_new_class_measured_and_reproduced.mechanism: validation/registry.py::_generated_by_pattern(symbol_names) exempts 'generated by this/the <noun>' only when <noun> is one of a fixed 6-word pipeline vocabulary (library/package/module/crate/tool/project) or an EXACT SUPPORTED public_symbol's own last dotted segment, lowercased (symbol_names, registry.py:1039-1043). The word immediately following 'the' in this sentence is 'clipping' (a gerund/verbal-noun), which is not itself any public_symbol's literal name - the real, verified class is spelled Clipper (public_symbol:aspose.page.ps.clipper.clipper, one of 167 SUPPORTED public_symbol facts under aspose.page.ps.clipper.*, e.g. Clipper, ClipperException, ClipType, IntPoint, OutRec, TEdge), and a separate real method aspose.page.common.render_model.RenderModelBuilder.clip also SUPPORTED. The exemption performs no stemming or morphological matching: 'clipper' and 'clip' are both members of symbol_names, but 'clipping' - the natural English word every one of this document's OTHER twelve api_reference sentences about the same subsystem also uses ('polygon clipping', 'during clipping', 'clipping algorithm', 'clipping operations') - is not, because none of those other sentences happen to be phrased as 'generated by the <word>'.

Calling the production repository_presenter.components.readme.validation.registry.narration_patterns(symbol_names)['generated by'] directly against the exact rendered sentence (lowercased) returns a match (i.e. BC-07 flags it) even when symbol_names is seeded with 'clipper'/'clip'/'outpt'/'outrec' - confirmed by direct interpreter call, not inferred from reading the regex alone.

proposal.for: the primary/supervisor - needs arrival-list admission before any lane or worker may land it
proposal.root_cause: The 'generated by this/the <noun>' exemption (G4-W17 items 22, 102/E20) recognises a real subsystem only by exact, literal string identity against a SUPPORTED public_symbol's lowercased final dotted segment. It has no notion that 'clipping' is the ordinary English gerund of the verified symbol 'clip'/'Clipper' - the identical class of gap items 102/103 already fixed twice for a missing noun ('tokenizer') and a missing punctuation guard (hyphen-continuation), now recurring a third time for a missing morphological form.
proposal.proposed_shape: Not prescribed here (the owner's choice among trade-offs, per the item 102/103 precedent of narrow, evidence-fitted widenings): (a) widen the match to accept a noun that shares a stem with a symbol_names entry (e.g. the candidate word starts with, or is started by, a >=4-character prefix of some entry in symbol_names - 'clipping'.startswith('clip') and 'clip' in symbol_names already, no new fact needed); or (b) keep exact-match discipline but also test the word against a small set of regular English suffixes stripped ('-ing', '-er', '-ed') before the exact-match lookup, mirroring _COMMAND's existing hyphen-continuation guard shape rather than growing the fixed 6-word list again. Explicitly not proposed: admitting every gerund unconditionally (would re-admit real pipeline narration spelled as a gerund, e.g. a hypothetical 'generated by the validating' - untested and not measured), and not proposed: touching the fixed 6-word _GENERATED_BY_NOUNS list itself, which this finding does not implicate.
proposal.explicitly_not_proposed: No relaxation of BC-07's other four sub-rules (H1 count, badge row, canonical abbreviations, length budget) and no change to the whole-phrase symbol_names exemption a few lines above (used correctly here - 'clipper' and 'clip' both already exempt themselves as bare narration matches; only the compound 'generated by the clipping' sentence fails). No new blocking check (rule 14) - this narrows an existing check's own false-positive surface, the same shape as items 102/103.
